Body: Related in the same family: #51223 (v2.0.16, Linux) — permission asks raised by MCP tools nested in Code Mode never surface in the TUI, so the call hangs until user interrupt (aborted with "Tool execution interrupted"). Includes full repro and a discriminating test showing config-allowed tools return in 31 ms while ask-gated tools hang. Might be worth checking whether the freeze here is also a permission check that never surfaces.

For reference, a fully-reproduced variant of the "Tool execution interrupted" symptom: #51223 (v2.0.16) — permission asks from MCP tools called inside Code Mode never surface in the TUI, so the execute call hangs and is aborted as interrupted on the next user input. May or may not be the same root cause here.
Bumping to show activity, even though it might be too late for this issue.

I am working on a related but distinct Desktop/Web case: the UI shows the final turn duration, but no live total while a long LLM inference, shell command, MCP call, or subagent is running. Per-tool timing in #50892 would not cover the total wall-clock interval across those steps. Older requests #27032 and #38666 were closed, and #38675 was not merged. I have a small frontend patch against current dev that starts on submit, ticks once per second near the composer, and freezes on completion or interruption; a production-build browser test covers a silent five-minute turn. Before opening a PR, would the team accept a persistent near-composer turn timer, or prefer another placement? I can adjust the patch to match the intended design.

Fix-size update: this is a one-line change, and I confirmed the fallback covers every locale rather than just English.

I simulated the real merge from `packages/app/src/runtime/i18n/language.tsx` against the shipped files - `base = { ...appEn, ...uiEn }` (`:88`) and the per-locale overlay `{ ...base, ...{ ...appLocale, ...uiLocale } }` (`:92`):

- as shipped: `base["ui.tool.todos"]` and `th["ui.tool.todos"]` are both `undefined`;
- after adding the key to `packages/ui/src/i18n/en.ts` only: `base` gets `To-dos`, and `th` also resolves to `To-dos`, because the locale overlay does not carry that key, so the base value survives the spread.

So the English entry is what removes `undefined` everywhere - a locale that has no translation shows the English string instead of crashing, and translations can follow separately. That also matches how the dictionaries are built: `packages/ui/src/i18n/th.ts` and `en.ts` hold the same 248 keys today, both missing this one, so the omission came from the source entry rather than from any single translation.

I reproduced both branches of `list()` with the same input to be sure the diagnosis is exact:

```
th  -> TypeError: Iterable yielded undefined which is not a string
en  -> "Read, , Shell"
```

The throw matches your report; the second line is the invisible half.

Two questions before I write it up:

1. Scope - the dictionary entry alone, or the entry plus hardening `list()` (`packages/ui/src/context/i18n.tsx:77-80`) so a non-string entry degrades instead of killing the whole timeline? The test for either belongs in `packages/ui/src/context/i18n.test.ts`, which currently covers `pluralCategory` and `tDynamic` only.
2. Translations - I would add the English entry and the languages I can write accurately, and leave the rest to fall back to English rather than machine-translate 60 files. Tell me if you would rather have the key present in every dictionary, even untranslated.

### Still reproducible on released v2.0.13 (verified 2026-09-25)

Fetched `https://opencode.ai/config.json` fresh today (39,039 bytes) — still generated from the V1 shapes:

- **`"servers"` → 0 occurrences** anywhere in the published schema JSON
- `mcp` def is the V1 flat map:

```json
"mcp": {
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": {
    "anyOf": [
      { "$ref": "#/$defs/McpLocalConfig" },
      { "$ref": "#/$defs/McpRemoteConfig" },
      { "type": "object", "properties": { "enabled": { "type": "boolean" } },
        "required": ["enabled"], "additionalProperties": false }
    ]
  }
}
```

- `$defs.McpLocalConfig.properties` = `type, command, cwd, environment, enabled, timeout`
- `$defs.McpRemoteConfig.properties` = `type, url, enabled, headers, oauth, timeout`

→ neither MCP def has `disabled`; the only `"disabled"` occurrences in the whole schema belong to unrelated defs (`variants`, `share`, `extensions`).

So a V2 config copied from https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/mcp-servers gets `Property servers is not allowed`, and per-server `disabled` gets `Property disabled is not allowed` — while the schema still suggests the removed `enabled` key.

**Environment:** opencode v2.0.13 (npm `@opencode/cli`, channel `latest`), Linux 6.17.0-40-generic, VS Code built-in JSON LS, fish. Reproduces consistently (JSON LS, no overrides).

**Workaround in use:** vendored patched schema + relative `$schema` path; will revert once the published schema ships the V2 shape.

I'll take this. Confirmed on current v2 — same mechanism, same silent drop: `matter(content)` in `packages/core/src/config/markdown.ts:6` is called without options, so gray-matter uses its module-global content cache, which it writes *before* parsing (gray-matter/index.js:47). A failed YAML parse leaves a poisoned entry, and every later `parse()` with the same content returns it without throwing — so the `sanitize()` fallback at markdown.ts:8 never runs and the skill is dropped by the empty-data check upstream.

Fix is one line: call `matter(content, {})`. Passing any options object bypasses the cache read and write (gray-matter only caches when called with no options), so every parse is deterministic and the fallback works on each load. Add a regression test that parses invalid frontmatter twice and asserts the second parse still throws (and the sanitized retry still recovers).

I can confirm this as well. The missing working directory and project/namespace context prevents the Duo workflow from having the repository context it needs. I also confirmed that an expired or invalid GitLab OAuth credential returning `invalid_grant` can cause provider initialization to fail and prevent OpenCode from starting.

_The following comment was made by an LLM, it may be inaccurate:_

Confirming this still reproduces on **2.0.16** (npm `@opencode/cli`, macOS arm64 — installed 2026-09-25). The highest version reported in this thread so far was 2.0.14, so the regression is still present in the latest release.

Setup here is a **config-only OpenAI-compatible provider** (no discovery plugin, no Ollama, no `auth.json` entry): `provider.<id>` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` with `npm: "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"`, inline `options.apiKey`/`baseURL`, and an explicit `models` map.

Observed on 2.0.16:

- ACP `session/new` → `configOptions[model].options` contains **zero** models from that provider, and `currentValue` falls back to a built-in (`opencode/*`, or `xiaomi/*` on a setup with other credentials stored).
- `session/set_config_option` with `model=<provider>/<model>` → `-32602 Invalid params: model not found: <provider>/<model>` (`data.providerId` is parsed correctly), so a client cannot select the provider even when it knows the id.
- Same build, same config: `opencode models` lists the provider's models and `opencode run --model <provider>/<model>` answers normally — ACP catalog only.
- List size is not stable across runs with an identical config: 7 / 8 / 17 / 19 / 20 options observed in isolated `XDG_*` sandboxes, and 95 (= providers from the models.dev catalog with stored credentials) on a long-lived setup. That matches the "poll exits before config-sourced providers activate" diagnosis above.

Client impact worth noting: an ACP client (Obsidian's Grimoire plugin) renders the `model not found` error as *"The selected OpenCode model is unavailable for this account or plan. Choose another model, then retry."*, which sends users chasing billing/plan issues instead of this bug.

Client-side workarounds: none for config-declared providers. Selecting a model that *is* in the catalog works in the same session, and the CLI is unaffected.

Extra data point that isolates this to the ACP catalog loader rather than config loading: on **2.0.16** (macOS arm64), with an intact config containing a config-declared OpenAI-compatible provider, the HTTP API and ACP disagree **at the same moment**:

- `GET /api/model` → 38 models including the provider's 5 (`{opencode: 8, xiaomi: 6, openai: 15, deepseek: 4, <custom>: 5}`), and `GET /api/provider` lists the custom provider with `activation: "enabled"`.
- `opencode acp` → `session/new` immediately after → `configOptions[model].options` = 95 models from `github-copilot` / `openai` / `xiaomi` only, custom provider absent (reproduced twice, ~2 min apart).

So config loading and provider activation do complete for the server; only the ACP catalog snapshot misses them (or misses them most of the time — the same probes returned 7 / 8 / 17 / 19 / 20 / 95 entries depending on run, which is why I think the poll-exit timing is the deciding factor rather than any file/config difference).

Worth noting for anyone debugging: `opencode reload` or a service restart does **not** change the ACP result, but the server's `/api/model` picks the provider up right away.
